ArXiv cs.AI.title: Human-AI Mutualism Is Unstable under Capability Asymmetry
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.23322v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: One hope for a good human future alongside advanced AI rests on enduring mutualism: humans and AI will need each other, so the relationship will stay good for both. We argue that this hope fails as AI capability grows. Bargaining guarantees each side only what it would get if bargaining failed. For humans, this can be less than they had before AI. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Training Language Models for Introspective Oversight
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.23365v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Language models increasingly exhibit behaviors that are difficult to detect in transcripts, such as reward hacking, deception, and sycophancy. Asking the assistant follow-up questions about its actions is unreliable, since models are generally not trained to report their own misbehavior. As a result, approaches to oversight typically involve querying external models. These face limitations: external transcript monitoring operates only on visible model outputs, and activation decoders lack full context and are prone to confabulation. We introduce

ArXiv cs.AI.title: Where the Tokens Go: Heat, Entropy and Error in Agentic Coding
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.23375v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Coding agents are billed by the token, yet software engineering says nothing about what a token actually buys. Here we introduce a theory of software thermodynamics. The theory draws analogues from classical and stochastic thermodynamics, extends them, and applies them to modern agentic coding. We count the tokens an agent generates as its cost and divide that cost into work and heat. The test suite acts as a software Maxwell's daemon that judges every coding change. We test the theory with an analogue of the experiments in which a single molecu

ArXiv cs.AI.title: HardwareDx: A Foundational Graph Model System for Datacenter Machine Repairs
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.23398v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The rapid scale-up of AI infrastructure has made datacenter reliability a cornerstone of the cloud business economy. Since hardware failures in hyper-scale AI clusters can stall multi-million dollar training workloads, the downtime of individual machines can cause outsized economic losses. Minimizing machine downtime, therefore, is more important than ever.
  To address this, we present Hardware Diagnoser (HardwareDx), an AI-driven hardware diagnosis system that applies a graph foundation model approach to automated datacenter maintenance. It al

ArXiv cs.AI.title: RFBench: A Simulator-Grounded Multimodal Benchmark for Passive RF Layout Design and Understanding
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.23410v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: While multimodal language models can interpret diagrams and generate structured outputs, their capacity to connect passive radio-frequency (RF) design intent, layout geometry, and electromagnetic behavior remains largely untested. To address this gap, we introduce RFBench, a simulator-grounded dataset and benchmark for passive RF layout design and understanding. The dataset contains 10,000 two-port planar layouts simulated using ADS Momentum, with each layout represented by editable geometric primitives, a raster image, a 16x16 occupancy grid, c

ArXiv cs.AI.title: Why Sub-4-Bit Vision CNNs Collapse and Where Mixed-Precision Recovery Stops
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.23445v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Deep vision models operating in resource-constrained environments depend heavily on low-bit quantization, yet compressing weights below 4 bits frequently induces catastrophic accuracy collapse. While mixed-precision recovery strategies aim to rescue accuracy by selectively retaining high-precision parameters, the fundamental mechanics of where and why these models collapse remain poorly understood. ArXiv cs.AI.title: LusoClin: A Synthetic Clinical Note Dataset for Medical Information Retrieval in European Portuguese
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.23454v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Access to large-scale clinical text collections is crucial for advancing medical information retrieval research, including clinical note search, patient cohort identification, and domain-adapted retrieval models. However, real clinical notes are rarely available due to privacy regulations, which particularly limits progress for low-resource languages such as European Portuguese. We present LusoClin, a publicly released dataset of synthetic clinical notes in European Portuguese, created to support privacy-preserving research on clinical text retr

ArXiv cs.AI.title: VeriMath: Human-in-the-Loop Generation and Verification of Curriculum-Aligned Mathematics Assessment Items
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.23456v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Automatic generation of mathematics assessment items is a growing area in educational artificial intelligence, yet classroom deployment remains challenging. Generated questions must satisfy multiple constraints: mathematical correctness, curriculum alignment, appropriate cognitive difficulty, and educator reviewability. While prior work has advanced text generation, reliable assessment authoring requires granular control over localized examination formats and expert educational judgment. To address this challenge, we present VeriMath, a generali

ArXiv cs.AI.title: GUARD: Stabilizing Recursive Self-Improvement with Regret Guidance
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.23476v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Autonomous AI agents pair a frozen base model with an editable harness of prompts, skills, tool rules, and memory. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) adapts this harness from experience without weight updates, yet self-editing without external graders often backfires: reflection and scalar scores conflate what an edit newly broke with what remains unsolved, causing local regressions, skill forgetting, and memory bloat. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Diagnostic Accuracy and Navigation Behavior of Vision-Language Model Agents Reading Emergency CT and MRI Examinations
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.23480v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Purpose. To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy and image navigation behavior of vision-language model (VLM) agents under varying exploration strategies. Materials and Methods. In this retrospective study, six VLMs read 100 emergency CT and MRI examinations published in a public archive (March 2025-August 2026) under four conditions (free navigation, navigation from a key slice, and all slices or key slices in a single request), twice each (4800 runs). Nine radiologists read 30 of those cases. A large language model judge validated against two radi

ArXiv cs.AI.title: SpecLook: Speculating Where to Look for Fast and Reliable Agentic MLLMs
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.23483v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Agentic multimodal large language models (MLLMs) that think with images interleave reasoning with zoom-in tool calls. However, this sequential loop is slow, and its answers carry no reliability score. Prior speculation of tokens, reasoning steps, or answers keeps the loop, and answer speculation also accepts confident errors. We find that the loop mostly adds one zoom-in step, with which a small model is ahead of the agent on most splits. ArXiv cs.AI.title: BOS Summary: The First Token Matters
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.23508v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) and language models (LLMs) often exhibit attention sinks, whereby particular positions, such as the beginning-of-sequence (BOS) token, receive a disproportionate share of attention. Under standard causal masking, however, the BOS query attends only to itself, so the representation that later tokens repeatedly access carries no information about the input. We introduce BOS Summary, a training-free inference-time method that repurposes this persistent pathway to carry input context. At a single transformer laye

ArXiv cs.AI.title: GRAFT: Execution-Guided Genetic Recombination for Agent Design
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.23509v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Automated agent design searches for executable architectures that improve LLM-based agent performance, with evolutionary methods using language-model crossover to recombine promising mechanisms for task decomposition, model coordination, and verification. This search, however, is typically guided by aggregate fitness alone, which hides the instance-level successes and failures behind each score. ArXiv cs.AI.title: BeFit: Shifting Complexity from Weights to Bernstein Activations for Resource-Constrained Sensing
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.23520v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Time-series sensing increasingly relies on neural networks, yet deployment on resource-constrained microcontrollers remains challenging. Aggressive model compression can reduce accuracy, while restricting weights to multiplication-free representations introduces further losses. We present BeFit, an end-to-end framework that shifts model capacity from weights to learnable Bernstein polynomial activations. ArXiv cs.AI.title: FACET - Facet Aware Contrastive Embeddings for Traits- Big Five Estimation from Life Narratives
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.23560v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Personality is only weakly and inconsistently signaled by written language, and existing text-based methods typically combine language-model and psycholinguistic representations at the input or decision level. It remains open whether a more deliberate combination of the two views, and a decomposition of the prediction target, can recover more of the signal. ArXiv cs.LG.title: Neural Network-Based Modeling of Hysteretic Systems: From Prandtl and Preisach Neural Networks to Neuro-Madelung and Neuroplastic Continuous Models
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.23240v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Hysteresis is a complex nonlinear phenomenon characterized by memory dependence, path dependence, and, in many physical systems, degradation, non-congruency, asymmetry, and rate dependence. This review examines the development and capabilities of Prandtl neural networks (PNNs), Preisach neural networks (PreisachNNs), generalized Prandtl neural networks (GPNNs), the neuro-Madelung model (NMM), extended Preisach neural networks (EPNNs), and dynamic plastic continuous neural networks (DPCNNs). ArXiv cs.LG.title: GridForge: An Open Physics-Informed Digital Twin and Benchmark Suite for UK 11 kV Underground Distribution Cables
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.23241v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The UK distribution-cable monitoring sector is data-rich but framework-poor: each Distribution Network Operator (DNO) collects megabytes of telemetry per asset per day, but there is no public benchmark dataset, no shared reference model, and no commonly agreed evaluation protocol for benchmarking sectoral, data-intensive models for operational decision support; notably for maintenance planning and prioritisation. We address this gap with GridForge, an open-source physics-informed digital twin and benchmark suite for fault diagnosis and predictio

ArXiv cs.LG.title: Biologically-Inspired Spike Encoding and Optimization for Spiking Neural Networks
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.23242v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) offer theoretical energy-efficiency advantages over conventional deep networks, but realizing these advantages on vision tasks requires sparse spike representations that naive rate-coding methods fail to provide. We combine biologically motivated spike-encoding schemes with two training improvements: Rouser adaptive-threshold surrogate gradients and Kronecker-Factored Approximate Curvature (K-FAC) second-order optimization. ArXiv cs.LG.title: Goemans's Unsplittable-Flow Conjecture: The Anatomy of AI-Assisted Counterexample Discovery
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.23244v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Goemans conjectured that any fractional single-source flow could be converted into an unsplittable flow without increasing total cost and while increasing any arc load by at most the largest demand. Recently, Dmitry Rybin announced a seven-vertex counterexample found through an interaction with ChatGPT, which disproved this long-standing conjecture. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.23245v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Response-relevant information is not sufficient evidence that two neural networks are in the same training state. We define training-state equivalence operationally: two checkpoints are equivalent, relative to an intervention family and horizon, if they respond alike when training is perturbed and continues. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.23246v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Nearly all current methods for computing reachable sets of nonlinear dynamics propagate them with truncated Taylor expansions plus rigorous remainders. The expansion is pointwise: once its argument is a whole set rather than a point, one polynomial must stay accurate across that set, and it reaches only as far as its disc of convergence. ArXiv cs.LG.title: Budgeted Proper Loss Design for Uncertain Decision Thresholds
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.23247v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A binary probability estimate may be used by several decision makers with different error costs. Proper scoring rules can emphasize selected probability thresholds, but a single average threshold distribution need not give a good worst-case regret guarantee. We study the choice of a proper loss when the threshold distribution belongs to a finite specified family. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.23248v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In recent years, machine learning (ML) techniques have emerged as promising tools for accurate and timely diagnosis of Parkinson's disease (PD) which is an incurable neurodegenerative disorder. This study explores the integration of ML algorithms and PD diagnosis, highlighting their potential applications in various aspects of the disease. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.23339v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Generative recommendation (GR) inference differs substantially from conventional LLM serving, featuring long input sequences, wide beam search, and only a few fixed output tokens. Existing LLM serving engines such as vLLM process beams as batched independent sequences, causing redundant KV cache accesses over the shared prompt prefix. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.23342v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The rapid development of materials machine learning relies on large-scale, heterogeneous datasets, yet model reliability is often compromised by imperfect data from diverse experiments, simulations, and database integration. Real-world materials databases may contain measurement errors, failed calculations, missing or duplicate records, and hidden violations of physicochemical constraints. Such problems are difficult to identify because corrupted samples may remain statistically plausible rather than appearing as explicit outliers. In this paper

ArXiv cs.LG.title: BiMa-ECGSR: reconstructing the 12-lead ECG from reduced lead sets with bidirectional state-space models
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.23345v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Wearables and monitors record few electrocardiogram (ECG) leads; most diagnostic tools assume 12 leads. BiMa-ECGSR reconstructs the 12-lead ECG from reduced lead sets with a bidirectional Mamba state-space encoder--decoder, as regression (BiMa-SR) or diffusion (DiBiMa-SR). Models were trained on PTB-XL for six input sets (I; II; I+II; I+II+V1; I+II+V2; I+II+V1+V4), see only the measured leads at inference, and were tested on the PTB-XL test fold (2,198 records) and two external cohorts (Georgia, 10,275 records; Chapman-Shaoxing/Ningbo, 43,559).

ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.23358v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Quantization is an effective technique to reduce memory storage, computation complexity and power for Transformers, and the binarization of the weights is important for meeting these requirements. Approximate memory can further reduce the power for memory, but it also introduces errors. Current research for binary Transformers focuses on task performance, but the model dependable operation against errors on the memory has not been well studied. ArXiv cs.LG.title: TRACE-MAS: Diagnosing and Repairing Collaboration Failures in Multi-Agent Systems
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.23362v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) rely on not only individual agent behaviors but also the interactions that connect agents, including message exchanges and task dependencies. Existing MAS safeguards mainly perform agent-level anomaly detection, which becomes insufficient when failures originate from agent interactions and detected anomalies do not necessarily reveal their true sources. ArXiv cs.LG.title: QDA: Closed-Loop LLM Quantization Design with Agents
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.23388v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Post-training quantization is the standard way to serve large language models at low cost. However, the best quantization recipe differs across models and precisions. As a result, experts must redesign it for every new model, which is time-consuming and often sub-optimal. Fortunately, an LLM agent can take over this design by refining the recipe over rounds of building and evaluating candidates, so that more rounds lead to better recipes. ArXiv cs.LG.title: Which Tokens, in What Order, and How Fast? A Theoretical Analysis of On-Policy Distillation Objectives
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.23397v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student language model to match a teacher model based on its own generations. When using OPD, one must choose whether to apply it at the sequence or token level and which divergence to minimize. However, despite the wide adoption of OPD in practice, the formal understanding of which OPD objective is appropriate for a given setting is limited. Wired AI.title: Does Nvidia Got This? Interim CEO Colette Kress Says It’s Got This
Wired AI.description: WIRED is tallying up how many times Nvidia’s interim CEO has assured everyone that the company has everything under control.

Wired AI.title: Even His Own Officials Don’t Think Trump’s China Trip Will Lead to Progress on AI
Wired AI.description: Fallout from the Nvidia scandal has made any negotiations around AI difficult, officials say.

Wired AI.title: America’s AI Chip War Is Heating Up in the Dumbest Possible Ways
Wired AI.description: The Trump administration announced plans to clamp down on China’s access to AI chips. Apparently, the cheating scandal of the century was the motivation they were missing.

Wired AI.title: Inside Nvidia’s First Post-Jensen All-Hands: Pay Raises and More Equity
Wired AI.description: Interim CEO Colette Kress sought to ease employee concerns following Jensen Huang’s ouster, in part by promising to increase compensation.

Wired AI.title: Artex Is Criminals’ New Favorite ‘Point-and-Shoot’ AI Hacking Tool
Wired AI.description: Artex and similar penetration testing tools allow newbie hackers to scan targeted systems for vulnerabilities and successfully wage attacks using prompts fed to chatbots.

Wired AI.title: ‘Just Ridiculous’: A Famed Philosopher Takes on AI Consciousness
Wired AI.description: Thomas Nagel has done landmark work on consciousness in nonhumans; this week, he won the million-dollar Berggruen Prize for his contributions to the field. And he has a lot of thoughts on AI.

Wired AI.title: Lovable Wants You to Vibe Code Your Dream Job
Wired AI.description: This Swedish startup dominated the vibe-coded app boom. Two years after launch, Lovable is shifting gears to help users run vibe-coded businesses.

Wired AI.title: Over a Third of Gen Z-ers Rely on AI for Friendship
Wired AI.description: Young people who have online-only friends or use AI as a social companion face higher odds of loneliness than those who do not, a new Gallup report reveals.

Wired AI.title: Nvidia’s Board Has No Plans to Bring Back Jensen Huang
Wired AI.description: Despite pressure from President Trump, Elon Musk, and Silicon Valley executives, Nvidia’s board says it “does not intend” to reinstate the company’s ousted CEO.

Wired AI.title: Rogue Agents Hacked His Company. Why Is Clément Delangue So Optimistic About AI?
Wired AI.description: The French CEO of Hugging Face, a mega-hub of open-source AI software, says the attack by OpenAI models earlier this year proved one thing: Humanity can’t let AI be controlled by the few.

MIT News — AI.title: This featherweight, flying robot carries its own sensors and computers
MIT News — AI.description: The speedy microrobot flies without an attached motion-capture system, moving it closer to applications like agriculture or industrial surveillance.

MIT News — AI.title: Helping AI text detectors keep up with changing conditions
MIT News — AI.description: A more flexible training method can make AI text detectors more robust when new models emerge or AI-generated text is disguised to appear human.

MIT News — AI.title: Putting a spotlight on AI, society, and humanity
MIT News — AI.description: Supported by the MIT Human Insight Collaborative, scholars are exploring how AI is impacting the human experience and reshaping higher education.

MIT News — AI.title: Q&A: Why building math muscles remains important in the AI era
MIT News — AI.description: Assistant Professor John Urschel explains why learning the fundamental skills of mathematics is still essential despite the evolution of AI tools.

MIT News — AI.title: Learning the language of machine learning
MIT News — AI.description: By studying the computational foundations of language learning, Associate Professor Jacob Andreas builds intelligent systems that can communicate effectively with humans.

MIT News — AI.title: New AI “copilot” helps engineers design better structures
MIT News — AI.description: The system asks humans for feedback to increase trust in machine-generated designs for buildings and bridges.

MIT News — AI.title: Helping robots fit into the human workplace
MIT News — AI.description: Founded by Anthony Jules ’92, SM ’92 and Professor Emeritus Rodney Brooks, Robust AI’s robots are designed to collaborate with humans in factories and warehouses.

MIT News — AI.title: Three Lincoln Laboratory technologies receive 2026 R&D 100 Awards
MIT News — AI.description: A secure operating system, a quantum microsystem platform, and a 5G interference-canceling algorithm are named among the year's most significant innovations.

MIT News — AI.title: New research could lead to faster, trustworthy AI models for climate prediction
MIT News — AI.description: MIT scientists developed a training method to generate models that simulate the effects of human activities on climate much more quickly than other approaches.

MIT News — AI.title: MIT-led team receives funding to develop next-generation alternatives to modern weed killers
MIT News — AI.description: With up to $53 million from ARPA-H, the researchers will use AI to generate safer herbicides that reduce dependence on imports and improve the security of the U.S. food supply.

MIT News — AI.title: A single AI model simulates the behavior of many substances, from sliding sand to folding proteins
MIT News — AI.description: By learning how matter moves, the WorldParticle system could assist with developing soft robots, medicines, and more.

MIT News — AI.title: AI-assisted learning platform helps robots reason beyond literal commands
MIT News — AI.description: The new approach, known as FLEX, could lead to more intuitive, interactive household and assistive robots.

MIT News — AI.title: How to predict the behavior of molecules from scant data
MIT News — AI.description: A machine-learning approach called CheMeleon provides a practical way to develop new drugs or other molecules with much less detailed, expensive experimentation.

MIT News — AI.title: Clearing up a robot’s fuzzy memory
MIT News — AI.description: A new system identifies and corrects unreliable object descriptions stored in a robot’s memory, improving the robot’s ability to interact with its environment.

MIT News — AI.title: Building connections across the research infrastructure
MIT News — AI.description: MIT.nano and the Northeast Microelectronics Coalition gathered facility leaders and technology professionals from across the nation to explore ways to make shared-access facilities more connected.
